milestones.title: Make automated classification decisions visible and correctable
Extend pinning to generated pipelines and reduce maintenance cost

items.title: Sign the release, obtain independent review, and publish cross-platform evidence
items.scope: release/release-manifest.json, signing infrastructure, independent review evidence, and hosted CI evidence
implementationSteps: Provision a trusted signing identity and record its public key fingerprint outside the repository.
Sign the release candidate and verify with npm run release:verify.
Commission an independent security review and record its signed result against the reviewed scope.
Run the cross-platform workflow on Windows, Linux, and macOS for Node 22, 24, and 26 and publish the aggregated evidence.
Clear each blocker in release/release-manifest.json only after its evidence artifact verifies.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run release:verify passes against a signed candidate.
reports/cross-platform-ci-evidence.json covers every required operating system and Node major.
SECURITY.md and README.md describe the achieved assurance rather than pending work.
verification: Verify the signature with the externally pinned fingerprint.
Confirm the independent review record binds to the reviewed scope and findings.
Re-run npm run check and the release verification chain.
items.rollout: Each blocker clears independently; no runtime change is required.
items.rollback: Reinstate the blocker in the manifest; the verification tooling already fails closed.
items.approvalReason: Introduces signing key custody and authorizes external publication of release evidence.
items.residualRisk: Signing keys require ongoing custody and rotation discipline.

items.title: Distinguish genuine coverage from shallow overlap in equivalence classification
items.scope: pso.mjs equivalence classification, adoption plan output, and adoption tests
implementationSteps: Add a coverage-depth signal such as relative content length or checklist-item count to the classifier.
Introduce an overlap classification that is reported but does not suppress installation.
Downgrade a match to overlap when the project's file is materially thinner than the framework template.
Print overlap and coverage separately in the adoption summary and record both in the plan.
Add fixtures for a thin existing instruction and a comprehensive one.

bestPracticeReferences.title: Customize AI responses in VS Code

acceptanceCriteria: A single-line existing instruction produces an overlap report and the framework template is still installed.
A comprehensive existing instruction still suppresses the framework template.
Both classifications appear separately in the printed summary and the plan.
--force-templates continues to install regardless of classification.
verification: Run the thin and comprehensive equivalence fixtures.
Confirm a rerun after adoption still reports zero changes.
items.rollout: Ship the overlap classification and reporting before changing what is suppressed.
items.rollback: Restore the current threshold; templates are only ever created when absent, so no existing project is affected.
items.residualRisk: Any depth heuristic can misjudge a concise but complete standard.

items.title: Report truncated stack scans and accept a declared stack on adopt
items.scope: pso.mjs stack detection, adoption plan output, adopt command options, and adoption tests
implementationSteps: Return whether the depth limit or entry cap was reached alongside the detected tags.
Record the truncation state in the adoption plan and print it in the summary.
Accept --stack on the adopt command and union it with detected tags.
Add a fixture that exceeds the entry cap and assert the truncation notice appears.
acceptanceCriteria: A repository exceeding the cap reports a truncated scan in the plan and the printed summary.
A normal repository reports a complete scan.
A declared stack on adopt installs the corresponding instruction files regardless of detection.
verification: Adopt with an explicit --stack and confirm the declared instructions are installed.
items.rollout: Additive reporting first, then the adopt-side override.
items.rollback: Remove the notice and the option; detection behavior is unchanged.
items.residualRisk: Repositories that legitimately exceed the cap will see the notice on every run.

items.title: Pin setup actions and toolchain versions in generated pipelines
items.scope: pso.mjs workflow generation, scripts/security-check.mjs, and adoption tests
implementationSteps: Verify the current commit SHA of the official setup action for each supported stack.
Emit the pinned action together with an explicit toolchain version for each stack.
Extend the template pinning rule so generated workflow content is checked with the same standard.
Assert in tests that every generated workflow pins both the action and the toolchain version.
acceptanceCriteria: Every generated workflow references only actions pinned to a full commit SHA.
Each supported stack pins an explicit toolchain version.
The pinning rule fails on a deliberately unpinned generated workflow.
verification: Generate a project for each supported stack and assert pinning.
Run a generated pipeline for at least one non-Node stack and confirm it succeeds.
items.rollout: Add one stack at a time as each SHA is verified; unverified stacks keep the current behavior.
items.rollback: Fall back to the runner-provided invocation for the affected stack.
items.residualRisk: Pinned action SHAs require deliberate maintenance to receive upstream fixes.

items.title: Decompose the runtime and add a dependency-free hygiene gate
items.scope: pso.mjs, a new internal module directory, package.json scripts, and the release file list
implementationSteps: Split the runtime along existing seams: detection, template planning, transactions, verification, inventory, and the command-line interface.
Keep pso.mjs as the single executable entry point and update the shipped file list accordingly.
Add a hygiene gate that runs without third-party dependencies, or record a documented development-only exception to the zero-dependency rule.
Refactor in small steps, running npm run check after each.
acceptanceCriteria: Each module has a single stated responsibility.
pso.mjs remains directly executable and the packaged distribution still installs offline.
npm run check passes with no behavior change.
The hygiene gate fails on a deliberately introduced violation.
verification: Run npm run check after each refactoring step.
Run the offline package installation test against the rebuilt candidate.
Confirm the hygiene gate detects a seeded violation.
items.rollout: Incremental, one seam at a time, each step independently revertible.
items.rollback: Revert the affected step; the entry point contract does not change.
items.residualRisk: A dependency-free hygiene gate is necessarily less capable than an established linter.

limitations: Ordering reflects security severity and user impact; no calendar dates or effort estimates are included.
REM-0101 is the only item requiring approval and the only one that depends on organizational process rather than code.
Items sharing a parallel group have no ordering constraint between them and may proceed concurrently.
No finding from this audit blocks use of the 1.0.0 candidate for authorized internal work.
This plan does not execute any remediation work; each item requires its own implementation pass and verification run.
